subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted `/exec` session defaults continue to override later `tools.exec` config, or should operator config become authoritative after config changes?
rationale: Current code and docs deliberately treat `/exec` as persisted per-session state, but the issue raises a real security-boundary concern when later stricter operator config is shadowed.

options.title: Make operator config authoritative
options.body: Change precedence or add migration/reset semantics so stricter `tools.exec` config reliably takes effect for existing Discord sessions.

options.title: Keep current per-session contract
options.body: Document the operational expectation more explicitly and rely on `/new`, `/reset`, session cleanup, or tool policy deny for enforcement.

options.title: Add explicit operator reset tooling
options.body: Preserve stored `/exec` precedence by default but add a doctor or session-reset command that clears stored exec fields after policy changes.

recommendation.title: Make operator config authoritative
recommendation.body: Change precedence or add migration/reset semantics so stricter `tools.exec` config reliably takes effect for existing Discord sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant `/exec` session override behavior and resolver tests trace most directly to steipete-authored history.
